To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lack of extracellular sodium ions in the presence of Ca2+ leads to mitochondrial swelling and to a loss of the ability of the mitochondria in cultured granule cells to sequester the cationic fluorescent dye rhodamine 12.

(i) the lack of extracellular sodium ions in the Ca2+-containing medium causes a Ca2+-dependent mitochondrial damage in cerebellar granules cells; (ii), the deleterious action of low sodium ions on mitochondria can be prevented by the blockade of NMDA receptor channels and by removing Ca2+ from medium.

the exposure of cultured neurons to SBSM results in the fact that Ca2+ ions de‐energize neuronal mitochondria and cause mitochondrial swelling, which can be prevented by the NMDA channel blocker, MK‐801, and the removal of calcium ions from the medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the mitochondrial dysfunction and damage in the neurons exposed to SBSM.
a possible role of the Na+/Ca 2+ exchanger in the regulation of the permeability transition pore in the mitochondria of cultured cerebellum neurons.
the role of the NMDA receptors in the regulation of the neuronal mitochondria functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Na+‐dependent Ca2+ influx into the cell via NMDA receptors is the major factor responsible for the mitochondrial dysfunction in cultured cerebellar neurons exposed to the low Na+ medium.

the lack of extracellular sodium ions in Ca2+‐rich medium leads to a Ca2+‐mediated damage of mitochondria in cerebellar granular neurons, which can be effectively prevented by NMDA receptor channel blockade.
the lack of extracellular sodium exacerbates Ca2+-dependent damage of cultured granule cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+ ions are the main mediators of the deleterious effects of SBSM in cerebellar granular neurons.
the Na+/Ca+ exchange mechanism is an important component of the cellular defence system against Ca2+‐overload in cerebellar granular cells.
the lack of extracellular sodium ions is deleterious for cultured cerebellar neurons and this damage is mediated by Ca2+ influx via NMDA receptors and the subsequent mitochondrial Ca2+ overload.
The main takeaway from our work is that
low Na+ in the presence of Ca2+ in the medium can cause mitochondrial dysfunction and cell death.
the lack of extracellular sodium ions can be a trigger for the neuronal death.
the lack of extracellular sodium ions is a powerful tool for studying the role of Ca2+‐mediated mechanisms in the regulation of neuronal functions.
